next_candidate: MiniMart Architecture Refinement v0.3 Freeze Candidate

findings.title: Cross-module query SQL contradicts the approved module-ownership rule
findings.evidence: v0.2 explicitly permits packages/query to execute approved read-only SQL/views or joins across schemas. The approved Reference Architecture states that modules communicate through typed interfaces/event bus and that no module reads another module's tables.
findings.impact: Freezing v0.2 would create an architecture exception that weakens a previously approved module boundary and can couple reporting/search directly to internal schemas.
findings.required: Remove direct cross-module internal-table reads. Cross-module reporting/search must compose public module query contracts or consume dedicated read models/projections built from public events/contracts. A projection may own its own reporting tables, but it must not treat another module's internal schema as its API.

findings.title: Reference Architecture technology baseline is not freeze-traceable and one explicit choice is weakened
findings.evidence: The v0.2 upstream list omits the approved Reference Architecture. Active v0.2 does not freeze Kysely/Drizzle, Vite/Tailwind, TanStack Query/Zustand, AG Grid Community/TanStack Table or UUIDv7, and changes the explicit pg-boss decision to 'pg-boss or equivalent'. OpenAPI+Zod is retained.
findings.impact: A v1.0 architecture freeze would no longer be sufficient to reconstruct the approved implementation stack, and coding agents could legitimately choose incompatible alternatives.
findings.required: Add an authoritative Technology Baseline/traceability matrix and carry forward every non-superseded approved choice: PostgreSQL; managed PostgreSQL; Node.js+TypeScript modular monolith; SQL-first Kysely or Drizzle; pg-boss; Tauri+React+Vite+Tailwind; TanStack Query+Zustand; AG Grid Community/TanStack Table; client-generated UUIDv7; OpenAPI+Zod; custom outbox/change-feed. Any intentional replacement requires an ADR.

findings.title: Edge/cloud runtime packaging no longer clearly preserves the same-service mode decision
findings.evidence: The approved Reference Architecture says the same service starts in edge or cloud mode and toggles modules/jobs. v0.2 presents Store and Cloud as separate composition roots without explicitly preserving one shared runtime service implementation.
findings.impact: The implementation could drift into two service applications with duplicated bootstrap/runtime behavior.
findings.required: State that edge and cloud use the same Node service runtime/composition framework with explicit mode/capability registration. Thin deployment launchers are acceptable; duplicated business/runtime implementations are not. Preserve the rule that cloud mode omits Store Posting authority.

findings.title: Approved security implementation baseline is weakened or omitted
findings.evidence: v0.2 says passwords/PINs are hashed and secrets use OS-protected storage, but does not retain the approved Argon2 choice, BitLocker store-machine baseline, signed installers/updates, dependency scanning or parameterized-SQL requirement.
findings.impact: Security-sensitive implementation choices would become optional during coding even though they were already approved.
findings.required: Restore these as explicit architecture requirements, while keeping SQLite encryption deferred with survival mode. Argon2 parameters/version must remain upgradeable rather than inventing fixed cost values.

findings.title: Phase-0 architecture risk gates are absent
findings.evidence: The approved architecture identifies Windows packaging/service registration/upgrades/rollback as the biggest technical risk and requires a Phase-0 spike; it also requires exact-printer testing for non-Latin raster receipts. v0.2 has deployment/hardware contracts but no explicit pre-feature architecture spike gate.
findings.impact: Development could start feature implementation before validating the highest-risk deployment and receipt/hardware assumptions.
findings.required: Add Architecture Validation Spikes: Windows installer/service/PostgreSQL upgrade+rollback; printer/scanner hardware; non-Latin receipt raster test on target printer; and minimal Store Node→Outbox→Cloud→Inbox/Dedup→ACK sync proof.

findings.title: Provider arrow in dependency diagram is directionally misleading
findings.evidence: diagrams/REFINED-ARCHITECTURE.md shows External Providers → Infrastructure while the prose correctly says provider adapters depend inward on MiniMart ports.
findings.required: Redraw the diagram so MiniMart adapter invocation of an external provider is distinct from inward code-dependency direction.

reference_architecture_evidence.module_read_rule: Each module owns its own tables and no module reads another module's tables (Reference Architecture v2 line 219).
reference_architecture_evidence.tech_stack: SQL-first Kysely or Drizzle; pg-boss; Tauri + React + Vite + Tailwind; TanStack Query + Zustand; AG Grid Community + TanStack Table; UUIDv7; OpenAPI + Zod; custom outbox/change-feed (lines 112-134).
reference_architecture_evidence.edge_cloud_mode: The same service starts in edge or cloud mode and toggles modules/jobs (line 246).
reference_architecture_evidence.security: Argon2; BitLocker; OS credential store; signed installers/updates; no card-number storage (lines 441-450).
